package_info.package_manager: Linux distribution package managers (e.g., apt, yum, pacman)
package_info.why_malicious: The xz package was compromised with a sophisticated backdoor in its liblzma component. The malicious code specifically targeted the SSH daemon (sshd) by hooking into its authentication routines, enabling attackers to bypass SSH authentication and gain unauthorized root access. This was a severe supply chain attack, as the backdoor was inserted upstream and distributed through official package repositories, affecting a wide range of Linux systems.

execution_context.trigger: When sshd is started and dynamically loads the compromised liblzma.so library
execution_context.file_location: liblzma/.libs/liblzma.so (built from the xz source tree in versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1)
required_permissions: process injection (to hook into sshd authentication routines)
network (to potentially exfiltrate data or enable remote access)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The malicious code is executed when sshd loads the compromised liblzma.so. It locates the sshd process in memory and patches its authentication routines, allowing the attacker to bypass normal authentication checks. This enables unauthorized root or privileged access to the system, effectively creating a stealthy backdoor.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: liblzma is a compression library and should not contain any code that interacts with process memory, authentication routines, or sshd internals. The presence of code that hooks into sshd and manipulates authentication is highly anomalous and indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate liblzma library is strictly limited to compression and decompression functions. It should not contain any process injection, memory patching, or authentication logic. The presence of constructor functions, process scanning, or authentication bypass code is a clear violation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None. There are no legitimate scenarios where a compression library would interact with sshd authentication or perform process injection.
key_indicators: Presence of __attribute__((constructor)) or similar initialization hooks in liblzma.so
Code that scans for or attaches to sshd process memory
Patching or replacing authentication-related functions within sshd
Obfuscated or non-standard C code blocks unrelated to compression
liblzma.so exporting unexpected symbols or containing additional ELF sections

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the xz/liblzma source code upstream by a compromised maintainer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of the compromised xz package through official Linux distribution channels

attack_chain.action: The compromised xz package (versions 5.6.0 or 5.6.1) is installed on target systems, replacing the legitimate liblzma.so library.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious liblzma.so is present on the system and will be loaded by processes using liblzma

attack_chain.action: When sshd is started, it dynamically loads the compromised liblzma.so, triggering the malicious constructor code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code hooks into sshd authentication routines

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits the backdoor to bypass SSH authentication and gain root or privileged access to the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise and potential lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: liblzma.so containing constructor functions or code that executes on library load
liblzma.so or xz package containing code that scans for or interacts with sshd process memory
Unexpected process injection or memory patching behavior originating from liblzma.so
Authentication bypass or privilege escalation events correlated with sshd and liblzma activity
file_indicators: liblzma.so with non-standard exported symbols or additional ELF sections (e.g., .note.xz-backdoor)
xz package versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 (or other known compromised versions)
Unexpected changes in the file hash or size of liblzma.so compared to known-good versions
Presence of obfuscated or non-standard C code in the liblzma source tree
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections initiated by sshd or liblzma processes
SSH authentication logs showing successful logins without valid credentials or with previously unknown keys
Unexpected remote connections to or from systems shortly after sshd startup
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of xz/liblzma versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes in liblzma.so, including unexpected symbols, ELF sections, or file size/hash mismatches. Analyze liblzma.so for constructor functions or code that interacts with process memory. Monitor sshd logs for anomalous authentication events, such as successful logins without valid credentials. Investigate any unusual outbound network activity from sshd or liblzma processes. Employ behavioral analysis to flag compression libraries exhibiting process injection, authentication bypass, or privilege escalation behaviors.
